title: Root administrative control of Grove's Liquidity Layer is held by Sky Governance, not by Grove Governance
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.1.1 defines the root of the permission tree and then names its holder: "The admin role (`DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE`) is the role that can grant and revoke **any** role, including itself and all other roles defined in the contract... This role is **fully controlled by Sky Governance via the Grove Proxy**." A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.3.1 repeats the arrangement for the Diamond PAU: the Default Admin Role "is held by the Grove Proxy."

This is the single most consequential fact about Grove's onchain autonomy. Every other role in the system — Relayer, Controller, Allocator, Freezer — exists because the admin granted it and persists because the admin has not revoked it. The admin can also reassign itself, so there is no configuration Grove could reach that the admin could not undo.

It means Grove's operational independence is **delegated, not owned**. Grove's governance decides what Grove does day to day; Sky Governance retains the ability to change who may do anything at all.

The pattern is consistent with everything else in the Artifact: Sky holds the supermajority of GROVE (A.6.1.1.2.2.1.4.2.1.2.2), the Core Council Risk Advisor gates risk-increasing proposals (A.6.1.1.2.2.2.2.2.1.2.4), the Core Atlas overrides the Grove Artifact (A.6.1.1.2.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6), and inherited operational logic propagates automatically. The admin role is the same relationship expressed in contract permissions.

The practical caveat is latency. Exercising `DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE` requires a Sky Executive Vote through the Proxy, which is slow — which is exactly why the fast, narrow Freezer Role exists alongside it rather than relying on the admin for emergencies.
description: DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE — which can grant and revoke every role including itself — is exercised through the Grove Proxy under Sky Governance control in both the monolithic and Diamond PAU implementations.
